subjective: Minnu, a male Indian cat, mostly indoor with occasional outdoor access, has had dark eye discharge for several weeks. He is generally active but has become anxious at night, vocalizing and disturbing sleep. Since last night, his lips and ears feel warm, and he is eating more than usual. He occasionally shows discomfort once or twice daily. He scratches his ears, and there is debris stuck in the ear canal. He has a history of liver infection and urinary tract infection two years ago. Stool is normal in color. No recent deworming; spot-on treatment (Salam) was applied yesterday.
objective: Physical examination revealed dark eye discharge that falls off when shaken. Temperature is normal. Stool color is normal. Ear canal contains wax and debris. No signs of severe distress noted. Weight approximately 5 kg previously, current weight not measured due to stress. No other abnormal physical findings reported.
assessment: Chronic dark eye discharge likely due to ocular or periocular irritation. Ear scratching and debris suggest otitis externa or ear infection. History of liver infection and urinary tract infection noted. Anxiety and increased appetite may be related to discomfort or stress. Salivation possibly stress-induced. No fever or systemic illness signs currently observed.
plan: Perform ear cleaning today and prescribe ear drops for 5-7 days. Instruct owner to gently wipe wax and debris before applying drops. Monitor ear for any growth increase or opening; surgical removal if necessary. Continue spot-on treatment for ectoparasite control; consider deworming for tapeworms. If symptoms persist or worsen, perform ear swab for culture and blood tests to rule out internal disease. Monitor appetite, behavior, and salivation. Reassess weight when possible. Owner to bring Minnu for follow-up if no improvement or if new symptoms develop.
conclusion: Minnu presents with chronic dark eye discharge, ear scratching with debris, and recent behavioral changes including nighttime anxiety and increased appetite. Physical exam shows normal temperature and stool, with ear wax accumulation. History includes liver infection and urinary tract infection. Treatment includes ear cleaning, ear drops, and continuation of spot-on ectoparasite control. Owner advised on ear care and monitoring for progression. Further diagnostics planned if no improvement. Weight monitoring deferred due to stress. Close observation recommended.
key_issues:
1. Chronic dark eye discharge with possible ocular irritation.
2. Ear scratching and debris consistent with otitis externa.
3. Behavioral changes including nighttime anxiety and increased appetite.
4. History of liver infection and urinary tract infection as relevant systemic considerations.
abnormal_findings: Dark eye discharge present for weeks. Ear canal wax and debris accumulation. Warmth noted on lips and ears. Increased appetite and nighttime anxiety. Occasional discomfort once or twice daily.
customer_instructions: Apply ear drops daily for 5-7 days after gently wiping wax and debris from the ear canal. Continue spot-on treatment as prescribed. Monitor for any increase in ear growth size or opening and report immediately. Observe Minnu's behavior, appetite, and salivation. Avoid bathing immediately after spot-on application. Bring Minnu for follow-up if symptoms persist or worsen. Monitor weight when possible and report any changes.
reminders: Follow-up if ear symptoms do not improve after ear drops and cleaning. Consider laboratory tests including blood work and ear swab culture if persistent symptoms. Monitor for any new or worsening clinical signs. Reassess weight when feasible.
